slides.headline: does *jupiter* really move backwards on saturday?
slides.dek: no. but the illusion is real, and it is pretty

slides.headline: “retrograde planets actually move backwards”
slides.body: no planet ever reverses its orbit. retrograde is how the motion looks from earth: we are moving too, so the planets seem to slow, stop and loop back against the stars.

slides.headline: it is the *overtaking* effect
slides.body: earth orbits faster than jupiter and saturn. when we pass them, they look like they drift backwards, the way a slower car seems to slide back as you overtake it on the highway.

slides.headline: retrograde reads as *review*, not disaster
slides.body: astrologers read a retrograde as time to revisit what that planet rules. saturn turns direct in aries on dec 10, and jupiter turns retrograde in leo on dec 12.

slides.headline: a planet looking backwards isn't a reason to *text* backwards
